title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering and regional failover thrashing
author: Anita Patel
description:
Summary: Fixes a race and ordering bug in the SLO Enforcer backoff scheduler that could cause regional failover + load-shedding to thrash under bursty cross-region load. This PR contains an emergency-stable change set intended to be low-risk: deterministic backoff ordering, smoother backoff decay (hysteresis), per-region token-bucket controls for load-shedding, and guardrails for fallback routing so downstream capacity storms do not cascade.

Background & motivation: During the 2026-02-18 incident (linked SUP-4382 / ENG-6821) we observed the SLO Enforcer flip-flopping regions when multiple regions hit transient overloads. The root cause was a combination of: 1) non-deterministic iteration order over region candidates that caused inconsistent backoff timestamps, 2) aggressive immediate decay of backoff on single successful probes causing rapid re-addition of regions (thrashing), and 3) an absence of per-region shaping for load-shedding which allowed a recovering region to accept bursts that immediately re-saturated upstream capacity. Together these produced repeated regional failovers and elevated error budgets.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Make region backoff queue deterministic: introduce an explicit priority order based on last-failure timestamp + region-stability score to avoid ordering races.
- Hysteresis on backoff decay: require N successful probe windows before fully clearing backoff for a region (configurable, default 3).
- Per-region token-bucket shaping for load-shedding: soft-rate limit to smooth bursts during recovery.
- Atomic update + locks around the backoff scheduler state to remove race conditions observed under heavy concurrency.
- Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate cross-region burst and validate no more than one failover per 30s window in canonical scenarios.
- Add metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_events, slo_enforcer.backoff_cleared, slo_enforcer.region_shaped_requests; update alerting runbook to account for hysteresis.

Risk & mitigation: Changes touch the SLO Enforcer core path but are designed to be conservative: defaults keep current failover thresholds and only add hysteresis and shaping. The new locking is scoped to the scheduler update path and avoids blocking request handling by performing rate-limited background reconciliation where possible. We added feature flags to enable/disable hysteresis and shaping per-deployment and included a short rollout plan below.

Testing & verification: Unit tests for ordering & lock; integration test that replays the production incident trace (see tests/enforcer/replay_test.go) and verifies stability; local soak for 24h on a canary dedicated pool. CI initially had a flaky timing test which was hardened by injecting a deterministic clock for tests (commit 2). All checks passed on rerun.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary cluster (dedicated/canary) with shaping disabled, observe metrics for 1h. 2) Enable per-region shaping + hysteresis on the canary; monitor slo_enforcer.backoff_events and request error rates for 6h. 3) Gradual rollout to 20% of traffic, then ramp. 4) If regressions seen, revert via feature flag (immediate).

Notes: This PR is intended as a hotfix backport candidate for the previous release branch if needed (ENG-6821 follow-up). The change is door-tested with the oncall and SRE runbook updates are included in docs/alerts.md.

review_comments: Diego Ramos (reviewer): The lock looks necessary but can we avoid blocking the hot path? Suggest using a short-lived mutex and move reconciliation to a background loop. Please add a comment describing why this is safe.

Author (Anita Patel): Addressed - mutex is short-lived and reconciliation moved to a rate-limited background worker; added comment and unit tests that assert request handler path latency stays within SLO under contention.

Author (Anita Patel): Added deterministic clock abstraction and updated flaky test; CI rerun passed (see ci_checks).

release_notes: Hotfix: Reduce SLO Enforcer regional failover thrashing by making backoff ordering deterministic, adding hysteresis to backoff clearing, and introducing per-region shaping. Adds metrics and runbook updates. Backwards-compatible; configurable via feature flags.
deploy_steps: Deploy to canary with shaping disabled
Observe metrics for 1 hour (slo_enforcer.backoff_events, error rate)
Enable shaping + hysteresis on canary, observe 6 hours
Full rollout and monitor for regressions
